objective: Demonstrate that the existing SECP structural FEA engine solves independent mechanical problems with exact analytical solutions and passes standard benchmarks before coupling into TwoWayFSICouplingEngine.
governanceRules: No duplicate FEM solver or parallel core created.
Used actual inspected component interfaces (StructuralAnalysisEngine.runFEA, GlobalAssemblyEngine, ElementFormulationEngine, MaterialModelEngine).
Separated three distinct domains: FEM engine existence, independent structural solver correctness, and multiphysics FSI coupling correctness.
Preserved partitioned Gauss-Seidel coupling architecture for future FSI integration.

stageA_ExecutionMap.reactionsAndEquilibrium: F_int = K_unconstrained * u, R = F_int - F_applied, equilibriumError = |F_net| / |F_applied|

stageB_AnalyticalTensileRodBenchmark.description: Prismatic rod under unconstrained axial tension fixed at x=0

cases.observedBehavior: Detected and rejected by FEAValidationEngine as non-physical rigid body mechanism

stageD_StaticForceEquilibrium.methodology: Exact unpenalized stiffness evaluation F_int = K_unconstrained * u; R = F_int - F_applied

stageF_IndependentBenchmark.benchmark: NAFEMS Standard 2D Quad4 Constant Stress Patch Test
stageF_IndependentBenchmark.details: NAFEMS Quad4 Constant Stress Patch Test PASS with exact state of constant stress across irregular interior node

limitations: Continuum 3D solid elements (TET4 / HEX8) require integration with SECP077CleanRoomKernel before full 3D solid qualification.

multiphysicsCouplingSeparation.notice: Independent structural solver qualification does NOT automatically qualify the fluid-structure interaction coupling loop.
multiphysicsCouplingSeparation.nextRequiredStep: SECP-ENGINE-QUALIFICATION-002-FSI-FEM-INTEGRATION-001: Invoke StructuralAnalysisEngine.runFEA within the partitioned Gauss-Seidel coupling loop in TwoWayFSICouplingEngine with Aitken dynamic under-relaxation, mapping interface forces and returning structural displacements.
